properties.name:
`design_holds` and NOT `design_updated`, deliberately — this file changed for a reason the other four did not share, and folding it in would have written a fiction into the ledger.

THE DESIGN WAS RIGHT AND THE CODE WAS WRONG, which is the definition of `defect_fix`. `structure.yaml` has always said a Component stores its descriptive text as `purpose`. `add_component`'s required-field resolver asked for a stored property called `description`, so the lookup missed on every existing Component and EVERY REVISE WAS REFUSED with "no such node exists yet to take it from" — about a node that `get_node` returned a moment later. Nothing in the design moved; the code now reads the property the schema always declared.

The other four artifacts in this same drift batch ARE `design_updated` against `chg:the-decomposition-ladder-is-open`, because there the design genuinely moved: a new `Project.decomposition_levels` property, `Component.level` changing from enum to string, a new `unknown_level` finding, and `Level` becoming `Ladder`.

Also added here: a regression test that asserts the PREMISE rather than the symptom — a Component has `purpose` and has no `description`. `Capability` is unaffected because it really does store `description`, which is why this survived and why a test covering only Capability would have stayed green.
